Key Takeaways
  • The NOC (No Objection Certificate) is a mandatory document issued by Nepal's Ministry of Education and Sports (MoEST) for all students planning to study abroad.
  • You can apply online at noc.moest.gov.np after receiving an unconditional offer letter from a foreign university.
  • The application fee is NPR 2,000, payable online via eSewa or at Rastriya Banijya Bank.
  • Processing typically takes 3–7 working days once all documents are correctly submitted.
  • The NOC is valid for 6 months from the date of issue — apply only when your visa deadline is near.
  • Language courses qualify only together with an academic course (Japan is the exception). Diploma-level courses have their own document list on the portal, so check the FAQ for your course type.
  • Without an NOC, Nepali banks cannot legally process international tuition payments or living expense transfers.

If you are a Nepali student planning to study abroad, you have almost certainly come across the term NOC. Yet surprisingly, many students begin their applications without fully understanding what this document is, why it matters, or — most critically — how to obtain it correctly. That oversight alone can delay your entire study abroad journey by weeks.

In this guide, Admizz Education walks you through everything you need to know about the No Objection Certificate for Nepal — from its purpose and eligibility to a step-by-step online application process and the most common mistakes to avoid. Whether you are heading to the UK, Australia, Canada, the USA, or anywhere else in the world, this guide applies to you.

What Is an NOC and Why Do You Need It?

An NOC, or No Objection Certificate, is an official document issued by Nepal's Ministry of Education and Sports (MoEST). In simple terms, it is the Nepali government's formal declaration that it has no objection to you pursuing education abroad at a specific institution, in a specific country, for a specific course.

However, the NOC is far more than just a piece of paper with a government stamp. It serves two critically important, practical purposes that affect every stage of your journey:

  • Financial Transfers: Nepali banks are legally required to see your NOC before processing any international tuition fee payment or living expense remittance. Without it, you simply cannot send money abroad through official banking channels.
  • Visa Documentation: Many countries — including the UK, Australia, and Canada — treat the NOC as a supporting document during student visa processing. It strengthens your application by demonstrating you have complied with your home country's requirements.
  • Legal Compliance: The NOC ensures your departure from Nepal is fully aligned with government policy, protecting you from any legal complications either at the airport or abroad.
  • University Requirement: Some foreign universities and scholarship bodies include the NOC in their list of required admission documents before finalizing your enrollment.
In short: Without an NOC, you cannot pay your tuition abroad, you may face issues with your visa application, and your departure from Nepal may be complicated. It is not optional — it is a foundational step in your study abroad process.

Who Needs an NOC from Nepal?

Before jumping into the application process, it is essential to understand whether you actually need an NOC. The answer, in most cases, is yes. Specifically, you must apply for an NOC if any of the following situations apply to you:

  • You have received an offer letter, CAS, or COE from a foreign university or institution.
  • You are enrolled in a bachelor's, master's, or PhD program outside Nepal. (Language courses must be paired with an academic course, except for Japan. Check the portal's FAQ for your course type.)
  • You need to transfer tuition fees or living expenses through a Nepali bank to a foreign institution.
  • You are a self-funded or sponsored student — both categories require an NOC.
  • You are applying for a student visa to any country, including the UK, Australia, Canada, the USA, Japan, or South Korea.
Check Your Course Type: The portal's FAQ says a language course must be paired with an academic course to get an NOC (Japan is the exception), and it lists separate documents for diploma, graduate diploma and degree courses. Rules can change, so always check the current FAQ at noc.moest.gov.np before you start your application.

Eligibility Criteria for NOC Nepal

Meeting the basic eligibility requirements is, of course, the first step before submitting your application. While these criteria are subject to change, the current MoEST guidelines for 2026 generally require the following:

  • Nepali Citizenship: You must be a citizen of Nepal, verified through your citizenship certificate or valid passport.
  • Completed Previous Academic Level: You must have finished your last academic qualification in Nepal or hold a recognized equivalent. For undergraduate applications, this typically means completing +2 (NEB) or A-Levels.
  • Minimum Academic Standing: MoEST may apply subject-specific benchmarks — for example, a minimum GPA of 2.4 in 10+2 for certain fields. Always check the current requirements on the official portal.
  • Valid Offer Letter: You must hold a valid, unconditional offer letter from a recognized foreign institution. The letter must state your name, course title, academic level, program duration, and full institution details.
  • Health-Related Courses: If you are applying for medicine, nursing, physiotherapy, public health, or a related field, you must first pass the Common Entrance Examination (CEE) and obtain an Eligibility Certificate from the Medical Education Commission (MEC) before applying for an NOC.

Documents Required for NOC Application

Gathering your documents in advance is arguably the single most important thing you can do to ensure a smooth NOC application. Importantly, all documents must be clear, correctly formatted (PDF or JPEG), and fully consistent with each other — particularly your name, date of birth, and passport number across all files.

🪪
Citizenship Certificate or Passport
Scanned copy in PDF or JPEG. Must clearly show your full name and date of birth.
📄
Offer / Admission Letter
Unconditional letter from the foreign university. Must include course, level, duration, and institution name.
📋
Academic Transcripts & Certificates
+2 (NEB) mark sheets and completion certificate, or equivalent prior qualifications.
🛂
Passport (if different from citizenship)
Required if your passport is your primary ID. Must be valid for at least the duration of your course.
🖼️
Passport-Size Photograph
Recent photograph against a white background, in digital format.
🏥
MEC Eligibility Certificate
Required only for health-related courses — medicine, nursing, physiotherapy, public health, etc.
🌐
English Translation (if applicable)
If any document from a foreign institution is not in English, it must be translated and verified by Bishwa Bhasa Nepal.
🧾
Invoice Letter
Listed in the portal's FAQ document list for diploma-level courses. Check the FAQ for your course type.
📑
Equivalence Letter (if applicable)
Needed if you passed your previous qualification in a foreign country.
🗂️
Copy of Previous NOC (if applicable)
Include it if an NOC has been issued to you before.
🗣️
English Test Certificate (if applicable)
The portal lists it if you are applying to New Zealand, or where it is applicable.
💳
Payment Receipt (NPR 2,000)
Proof of fee payment via eSewa, online banking, or Rastriya Banijya Bank cash deposit.
Pro Tip: Before you begin uploading, double-check that every document uses the exact same spelling of your name and the same date of birth. Even a minor mismatch between your citizenship and offer letter can result in rejection or delays. Consistency across all documents is non-negotiable.

How to Apply for NOC Online — Step-by-Step

The good news is that the entire NOC application process can now be completed online through the official MoEST portal. As a result, you no longer need to make multiple trips to Bhaktapur unless specifically required for in-person verification. Here is exactly how to do it:

🔗
Official Application Portal
noc.moest.gov.np
Ministry of Education and Sports — Foreign Study Permit Branch
1
Visit the Official MoEST NOC Portal
2 minutes
Go to noc.moest.gov.np and click on "Sign Up" or "NOC Application." Do not use any third-party websites claiming to process NOC applications — always use the official MoEST portal directly to avoid fraud.
2
Create Your Account with OTP Verification
5 minutes
Register using your email address and mobile number. You will receive a One-Time Password (OTP) on your phone to verify your account. After logging in, complete your profile by entering your full personal details, then verify your email address using the token sent to your inbox. The portal asks for an NTC (Nepal Telecom) mobile number to begin.
3
Fill in the Online Application Form
15–20 minutes
Select your intended country, university, program level (bachelor's, master's, PhD), and subject or stream. Enter all details exactly as they appear in your offer letter — including the institution name, course title, and start date. If your institution is not listed, request to have it added through the portal.
4
Upload Your Required Documents
10–15 minutes
Scan and upload all required documents in the correct format (PDF or JPEG). Ensure each file is clearly legible, properly named, and complete. Blurry, cropped, or incorrect documents are the most common reason for NOC rejection — so review each file carefully before uploading.
5
Submit Your Application and Track Status
Immediately
Once you submit, you will receive a confirmation number. Use this to monitor the status of your application on the portal. The MoEST team will review your documents and may contact you if anything requires clarification. At this stage, avoid submitting multiple applications for the same intake — it will delay processing.
6
Pay the Application Fee of NPR 2,000
After approval notification
Once your application is approved, you will be prompted to pay the NPR 2,000 fee. You can pay online via eSewa or online banking, or deposit cash at any branch of Rastriya Banijya Bank (RBB). Note that an additional NPR 2,000 applies if you need to make changes (such as a new course or institution) after submission.
7
Collect or Download Your NOC
3–7 working days after approval
After successful payment, your NOC will typically be ready within 3–7 working days. In many cases, you can download it directly from the portal. If in-person collection is required, visit the Foreign Study Permit Branch at Sanothimi, Bhaktapur. Bring your original documents for verification when collecting in person.
"Think of the NOC not as a bureaucratic hurdle, but as the foundation of your study abroad journey. Get it right from the start, and everything that follows — your visa, your tuition payments, your departure — becomes significantly smoother."

Common Mistakes That Delay NOC Applications

Unfortunately, a significant number of NOC applications are either delayed or rejected due to avoidable mistakes. Understanding these pitfalls in advance, therefore, is just as important as following the correct process. Here are the most frequent errors — and exactly how to avoid each one:

❌
Name or Date of Birth Mismatch Across Documents
If your name on your citizenship certificate differs even slightly from your offer letter (for example, "Sita Sharma" vs "Sita K. Sharma"), MoEST will flag your application. Fix: Ensure absolute consistency across all documents before uploading. If necessary, request a corrected offer letter from your university.
❌
Submitting a Conditional Offer Letter
A conditional offer means you have not yet met all entry requirements. MoEST requires an unconditional offer before issuing an NOC. Fix: Wait until you receive your final, unconditional offer — or a confirmation of enrolment — before beginning the NOC process.
❌
Blurry, Incomplete, or Incorrectly Formatted Documents
Uploading low-quality scans, files in the wrong format, or documents that cut off key information is one of the most common reasons for delays. Fix: Scan documents at a minimum of 300 DPI, check each file for clarity, and ensure they are in PDF or JPEG format as specified on the portal.
❌
Entering Course or Country Details Incorrectly in the Form
A mismatch between what you enter in the application form and what appears in your offer letter is a guaranteed way to have your application rejected. Fix: Cross-reference every field in the application form against your offer letter before submitting. Pay particular attention to the course title, program level, and institution name.
❌
Applying Too Late Before Your Visa Deadline
Because the NOC can take up to 7 working days — and sometimes longer during peak periods — leaving your application to the last minute can jeopardize your entire visa timeline. Fix: Apply for your NOC at least 4–6 weeks before your visa submission deadline. Do not assume it will be issued in 2 days.
❌
Submitting Multiple Applications for the Same Intake
Some students, in a panic, submit duplicate applications thinking it will speed up the process. In reality, it creates confusion and further delays. Fix: Submit one application and use the tracking feature on the portal to monitor its progress. If there is a genuine issue, contact MoEST directly through the official email or phone number.

MoEST Office Details and Contact Information

While the online portal handles most of the process, it is useful to have the official contact details on hand — particularly if you need to follow up on a delayed application or attend for in-person verification.

  • Office Name: Ministry of Education and Sports (MoEST) — Foreign Study Permit Branch
  • Office Address: Sanothimi, Bhaktapur, Nepal
  • Email: info.noc@moest.gov.np
  • Phone: +977 1-6635419
  • Office Hours: Sunday to Friday, 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM (closed Saturdays and public holidays)
  • Online Portal: noc.moest.gov.np
Beware of Fraudulent Services: Several third-party websites claim to process NOC applications on your behalf for a fee. MoEST does not authorize any such service. Always apply directly through the official portal at noc.moest.gov.np to protect yourself from fraud and ensure your application is processed correctly.

Your NOC Is Just the Beginning

Obtaining your NOC is, without doubt, a critical milestone in your study abroad journey — but it is also just one of many important steps. Once you have your NOC in hand, you will still need to finalize your student visa application, arrange accommodation, transfer tuition fees, book flights, and prepare for an entirely new chapter of your life in a foreign country.
